pr.title: [Merged by Bors] - feat(to_fun): throw a warning instead of creating a duplicate declaration
pr.body:
I noticed that people using the `to_fun` attribute were having a hard time realizing that the attribute didn't do anything in some cases. So, if the declaration type is unchanged, throw an error.

One such existing case has been uncovered in this PR.

files.patch:
@@ -160,7 +160,7 @@ theorem HasTemperateGrowth.comp' [NormedAddCommGroup D] [NormedSpace ℝ D] {g :
     _ = _ := by rw [mul_pow, ← pow_mul, pow_add]; ring
 
 /-- Composition of two temperate growth functions is of temperate growth. -/
-@[to_fun (attr := fun_prop)]
+@[fun_prop]
 theorem HasTemperateGrowth.comp [NormedAddCommGroup D] [NormedSpace ℝ D] {g : E → F} {f : D → E}
     (hg : g.HasTemperateGrowth) (hf : f.HasTemperateGrowth) : (g ∘ f).HasTemperateGrowth := by
   apply hf.comp' (t := Set.univ)

@@ -42,7 +42,10 @@ initialize registerBuiltinAttribute {
       throwError "`to_fun` can only be used as a global attribute"
     addRelatedDecl src "fun_" "" ref stx? (docstringPrefix? := s!"Eta-expanded form of `{src}`")
       fun value levels => do
-      let r ← Push.pullCore .lambda (← inferType value) none
+      let type ← inferType value
+      let r ← Push.pullCore .lambda type none
+      if r.expr == type then
+        throwError "`@[to_fun]` failed to eta-expand any part of `{.ofConstName src}`."
       return (← r.mkCast value, levels)
   | _ => throwUnsupportedSyntax }

@@ -10,7 +10,7 @@ theorem Function.mul_comm (f g : ℝ → ℝ) : f * g = g * f := _root_.mul_comm
 
 /-- Look I am the doc-string of `foo`. -/
 @[to_fun]
-theorem foo : 1 = 1 := rfl
+theorem foo : (1 : Nat → Nat) = 1 := rfl
 
 open Lean in
